props.question: Why does the room seem to stretch?
props.answer: The lens zooms in while the camera pulls back, so the subject holds its size and the background rushes away.

props.question: If the camera pulls back at the same rate as the lens zooms in, why does anything in the frame change at all?
props.answer: Because zooming magnifies everything by the same amount, while moving the camera changes the size of near things far more than far ones. The two cancel only at the distance of the subject. Everything behind it grows, everything in front of it shrinks, and the eye reads that as the room itself changing shape, which no real room does, and that is where the dread comes from.

item.title: Five days of amoxicillin against ten
item.text: Children aged six months to five years with pneumonia that did not need hospital care were given amoxicillin for five days or for ten. In all, 824 children were randomised across nine clinics. Treatment had failed by day 30 in 12.6% of the five-day group and 12.4% of the ten-day group, a difference well inside the margin set in advance. Side effects were mild and no more common in either group, and parents in the shorter arm missed fewer days of work. The authors conclude that five days is enough for a child treated at home, and that guidelines asking for longer should be revisited.
